cases.candidate_question: Reversing the integration direction leaves every line integral unchanged.
cases.why_invalid: For the coordinate form dx_i along a coordinate segment from a to b with a≠b, the two integrals are b-a and a-b, which are unequal.

cases.candidate_question: The splitting identity is valid for totalized integrals without any integrability assumptions.
cases.why_invalid: On [-1,1], take a scalar pullback equal to 1/|t| for t<0 and 1 for t>0. The integrals on [-1,0] and [-1,1] totalize to zero because they are not integrable, while the integral on [0,1] is 1; hence 0+1≠0.

cases.candidate_question: A line integral of an exact one-form is independent even of the order of its endpoints.
cases.why_invalid: Exactness removes dependence on the intervening path, not on endpoint order: this coordinate-family integral is b-a and changes to a-b on reversal.

cases.candidate_question: The endpoint difference equals the first integral alone, with no second velocity contribution.
cases.why_invalid: In dimension one take B(x,y)=xy, c(t)=d(t)=t and [a,b]=[0,1]. The first integral is 1/2 but the endpoint difference is 1; the second integral supplies the missing 1/2.
